*   DebugText must provide a constructor DebugText::new(leading: &str, expression: &str, trailing: &str) -> Self that takes all three text components. The previously public fields leading and trailing must be replaced with private storage and public getter methods.

*   DebugText must expose getter methods leading() -> &str, expression() -> &str, and trailing() -> &str that return references to the respective text components.

*   The formatter normalizer in crates/ruff_python_formatter/tests/normalizer.rs must be updated to use debug.leading(), debug.expression(), and debug.trailing() accessor methods (not direct field access), and must reconstruct DebugText using ast::DebugText::new(&leading, &expression, &trailing).

*   The duplicate union member check (PYI016) must compare f-string literals by their full source text representation, including the expression source text and any debug specifier. Two f-strings that produce different runtime output must NOT be flagged as duplicates.

Done. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Changes

**`crates/ruff_python_ast/src/nodes.rs`** — Refactored `DebugText`:
- Fields `leading`, `expression`, `trailing` (in that order) are now **private** `String`s. The new `expression` field stores the expression's verbatim source text.
- Added `DebugText::new(leading: &str, expression: &str, trailing: &str) -> Self`.
- Added getters `leading()`, `expression()`, `trailing()` returning `&str`.
- Kept the derived `Debug`, which now prints the three fields in declaration order (`leading`, `expression`, `trailing`) as required.

**`crates/ruff_python_parser/src/parser/expression.rs`** — The parser now captures the expression's source slice and builds the struct via `ast::DebugText::new(...)`.

**`crates/ruff_python_codegen/src/generator.rs`** and the two formatter files (**`string/mod.rs`**, **`other/interpolated_string_element.rs`**) — Updated to use the `.leading()` / `.trailing()` getters instead of direct field access.

## Why this fixes PYI016

PYI016 compares union members via `ComparableExpr`, whose interpolation nodes hold a `&DebugText`. Because `DebugText` now carries the expression source text, two self-documenting f-strings that yield the same AST but differ in source (e.g. `f"{0x0=}"` vs `f"{0o0=}"`, `f"{00=}"` vs `f"{000=}"`) — which produce different runtime output — now compare unequal and are no longer flagged. I verified end-to-end with `ruff check --select PYI016`:

- **Not flagged:** `f"{x =}"|f"{x=}"`, `f"{0x0=}"|f"{0o0=}"`, `f"{00=}"|f"{000=}"`, `f"{x=}"|f"{x}"`, `f"{x:.2f}"|f"{x:.3f}"` ✓
- **Flagged:** `f"{x=}"|f"{x=}"`, `f"{x}"|f"{x}"` ✓

## Note on the test file

Per the **CRITICAL** instruction, I did **not** modify `crates/ruff_python_formatter/tests/normalizer.rs` (it lives under `tests/`); the verification system will apply that patch, which updates it to use the new getters and `DebugText::new`. All source crates build cleanly, and a formatter roundtrip on self-documenting f-strings is preserved.
